analysis: Reviewed the three units plus the replayed workflow, CI and changelog patches. The change is mostly CI, docs, tests, and cluster-wizard plumbing. The substantive security change is in release-provider.yml: a new step computes cluster_runtime facts from the final signed app, and prepare conditionally adds --cluster-runtime (head ~1078-1088) when CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND is true. The workflow's containment controls are visible: the step deletes the signing keychain and proves the identity is gone, re-checks the bundle SHA-256 against BUNDLE_HASH, unsets r2_public_url and coordinator_url, reads no secrets.*, and runs the app CLI with an empty environment (env -i, per the workflow comment). Sending is opt-in per environment and fails closed when enabled; otherwise it only warns. upload-artifact is pinned by SHA and retains facts for 30 days. I found no secret exposure. The single finding is a trust and threat-model gap: build-produced facts, authenticated only by the release key (A-005), feed coordinator approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications (A-017, T-052, T-054). The coordinator's handling is platform-owned and unverified. Unit 1's production changes (strict v2 ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts parser, serving-scope defaults to .publicServing, MTP auto turned off for coordinator pairs, a retry of the approval set-aside after an hour, a per-part heartbeat file) looked conservative or availability-related, with no regression. Unit 2's tests pin schema, size and --cluster-runtime constraints. Unverified because the code was not supplied: scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, provider-cluster-runtime-models.py, the provider-release-publication.py handling, the coordinator validation, and the bodies of discoveryMode, setAside and partHealthPath permissions. T-041 is unaffected. The PR also drops auto-update for cluster pairs (a patch-currency concern for T-054/T-043). Human review of the coordinator contract is warranted.

findings.detail: The new CI step (.github/workflows/release-provider.yml, head ~941-1023; CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND at ~298-308) computes cluster_runtime facts with the freshly built app's own CLI and worker. When the per-environment variable is true, prepare adds --cluster-runtime (head ~1078-1088) and the block goes in the POST /v1/releases payload. The workflow comments and docs say the coordinator derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications of declared public models (ClusterPublicModels) from it. The facts are self-reported by the build and authenticated only by the release key. A holder of the release API key (A-005), or anyone who can alter the build-side declaration, could therefore create public-serving qualification, not only binary trust. That weakens the independent-qualification assumption behind A-017, T-052 and T-054. The coordinator-side controls are outside the supplied evidence and unverified. Fix: record this derivation path in the threat model, and confirm the coordinator requires independent approval of the cluster_runtime block rather than trusting the release key alone.
findings.title: Release-registered cluster_runtime can mint public-traffic cluster approvals, grants and parity qualifications; threat model does not cover it
